prompt:
A traditional East Asian ink-wash painting (sumi-e) on one plain sheet of warm, light rice paper with fine fibres, seen flat from straight above, evenly lit, no shadow, no frame, no table, no text, no signature, no red seal, no stamp. Paint it the way a master ink painter works: a few confident, loose brush strokes, wet ink bleeding softly into the paper, dry-brush texture where the brush runs out, simplified forms that suggest rather than describe, lots of white paper. It must look like a painting, expressive and artistic, with the brushwork of the reference picture: never a realistic drawing, never a detailed illustration, never a pencil sketch, never a 3D render. Copy only the reference's brushwork, never its subject: no bird, no crane, no reeds, no water, no landscape. Sumi ink only, from deep black to soft grey washes, plus real gold leaf only where stated. Generous empty paper on every side. The subject fills most of the picture (about 85% of its height and width): bold, generous, never small in the middle of empty paper.

A calm stream seen from slightly above, painted as a few horizontal strokes of soft grey wash, crossing the picture. Across it, a path of flat stepping stones leads from the near bank at the lower left to the far bank at the upper right: each stepping stone is an old closed book lying flat on the water, seven books, the nearest the largest, getting smaller with distance, each a few bold strokes with dry-brush page edges, a soft reflection under each. Quiet and clear: each book is one step forward. No gold, nothing readable, no people.
